gaps.text: outside supported scope: Line pressure and flow rate are physical process quantities that optical spectroscopy as described in the supplied sources cannot measure; they belong to pressure and flow instrumentation, not to the fiber-optic spectroscopic methods covered here. A spectroscopic contribution is conceivable only for the blockage early warning, as a hypothesis to test.
In-line measurement of Line pressure with pressure transducer
In-line measurement of Flow rate with flow meter
In-line measurement of Temperature at the measurement point with temperature sensor

items.finding: Distributed fiber optic sensing techniques using FBG systems can address pipeline issues such as blockages and structural integrity monitoring.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests testing distributed fiber sensing as a complementary method specifically for early blockage warning, while keeping pressure and flow measurement to dedicated standard instrumentation.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited study evaluates structural health monitoring in composite pipelines using numerical models and FBG sensors, which may differ significantly from metallic or industrial slurry transfer pipes.

citation.quote: Nikles and Briffod [19] introduced a technique to address the impact of blockages in hydrocarbon pipelines using a Fiber Bragg grating (FBG) sensing system which provides distributed sensing capabilities.
